`dml_from_drdid()` combines a panel DRDID ATT and its full unit-level influence
function with cross-fitted estimates of the conditional ATT sensitivity moments.
It returns a `dml_drdid` object inheriting from `dml`, so `dml_bounds()`,
`confidence_bounds()`, `robustness_value()`, `sensemakr()` and `dml_benchmark()`
can use the hybrid result.

## Supported scope

The adapter supports two-period balanced panels,
`estMethod = "imp"` or `"trad"`, and constant positive sampling weights. It requires `inffunc = TRUE`. Active source trimming,
source probability clipping, and DML probability clipping are rejected. The
improved estimator must use successful IPT estimation (`ps.flag` 0 or 1).

Repeated cross-sections, unequal sampling weights, clustered inference,
subgroup ATTs, active trimming and joint
bootstrap inference need separate extensions. A source fit estimated with
bootstrap standard errors can be supplied, but the adapter reports analytic
joint-IF inference; it does not reuse the source bootstrap draws or SE.

Acceptance checks the input, required DRDID function interfaces and numerical
ATT/IF reconstruction. DRDID **1.3.0** is tested; other versions must pass the
same checks. Installed versions are recorded for diagnostics, not used as
acceptance gates or evidence of the version that produced a historical fit. Reproducing the ATT
and ordered IF is a consistency check, not independent proof of historical
sample provenance or statistical assumptions.

## Inputs and alignment

For long input, supply `data` and the original outcome, time, ID and treatment
column names, covariate formula and any weight column. Literal names and literal
formulas can be recovered from `fit$call.param`; symbols referring to caller
variables must be resolved explicitly by the user. There are exactly two rows
per unit, with unique ID-time pairs and complete estimation variables. IDs and
times are numeric, following DRDID's preprocessing requirements. Treatment,
covariates and weights must be time invariant. The adapter uses DRDID's own
preprocessing and canonical sorted unit order.
Raw weights are checked before DRDID normalizes them; they must be numeric,
finite, strictly positive and equal across all supplied rows.

For wide input, supply `y1`, `y0`, `D`, `covariates`, and any `i.weights` in the
same unit order as `att.inf.func`. The design matrix includes whatever intercept
was used by DRDID; `covariates = NULL` denotes an intercept-only source model.
Optional `unit_id` labels the supplied rows but cannot independently identify
which historical row generated an influence-function entry.

The adapter re-estimates DRDID and checks the ATT and **ordered** IF against the
supplied result before estimating the sensitivity moments. It never silently
drops observations to make a fit pass. Model-matrix columns and grouped columns
are the units of benchmarking; an intercept column must be retained when all
other regressors are removed.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
source_fit <- DRDID::drdid(
  yname = "y", tname = "time", idname = "id", dname = "D",
  xformla = ~ x1 + x2, data = panel_data,
  panel = TRUE, estMethod = "imp", inffunc = TRUE
)

hybrid <- dml_from_drdid(
  source_fit, data = panel_data,
  dml_args = list(yreg = "lm", dreg = "glm", d.class = TRUE,
                  cf.folds = 3, cf.reps = 3, cf.seed = 17, ps.trim = 0)
)
summary(hybrid)
dml_bounds(hybrid, cf.y = 0.08, cf.d = 0.06)
confidence_bounds(hybrid, cf.y = 0.08, cf.d = 0.06)
robustness_value(hybrid)
benchmark <- dml_benchmark(hybrid, "x2")
benchmark_bounds(hybrid, benchmark)
```

The learners above illustrate a small correctly specified parametric example.
They are not a universal nuisance-model recommendation. `dml_args` accepts DML
learner specifications and training options. The adapter fixes `model = "npm"`,
`target = "att"`, `conditional = TRUE`, `centered = FALSE`,
`dirty.tuning = FALSE`, and `y.class = FALSE`. Hyperparameter tuning, if requested,
therefore takes place within the training folds. The default seed is 1 and the
default number of folds is 5. `cf.reps` defaults to 1 and accepts positive
integers up to the DML seed-pool size of 1,000,000. Omitted `yreg` and `dreg` inherit `reg`, which
defaults to `"ranger"`. For a constant-only design, unspecified predictor
preprocessing is set to `"ignore"`, since range scaling has no scale to estimate.
Explicit learner and preprocessing choices are preserved.
A specified probability threshold is allowed only
when it does not clip any fitted probabilities. Setting `ps.trim = 0` does not
make boundary predictions or poor overlap acceptable.

A complete simulated example for both long and wide inputs is installed at
`system.file("examples", "drdid-adapter.R", package = "dml.sensemakr")`.

## Repeated cross-fitting

Set `dml_args$cf.reps` to repeat the fold partition. Every repetition keeps the
same external ATT and IF and uses its own DML sensitivity moments and joint
covariance. No repetition is silently discarded: an invalid fold, active
trimming or invalid moment rejects the fit.

`results$main$treat[[r]]`, `fits[[r]]` and `auxiliary_dml_results$main$treat[[r]]`
refer to repetition `r`. `adapter_info$rep_seeds` records all seeds;
`fold_id` is a unit-by-repetition matrix when `cf.reps > 1` and remains a vector
for one repetition. `dml.att` records each auxiliary ATT before replacement.
Benchmarks refit both estimators on the same units and every saved partition.

Use `combine.method = "median"` (default) or `"mean"` with `confidence_bounds()`,
`robustness_value()`, `sensemakr()` and benchmark summaries/bounds. Each endpoint
is computed per repetition before aggregation. For endpoints `b_r` and SEs `s_r`,
the mean rule reports `mean(b_r)` with SE
`sqrt(mean(s_r^2 + (b_r - mean(b_r))^2))`; the median rule replaces both means by
medians. There is no division by the repetition count. The unchanged source ATT
and its analytic SE therefore remain unchanged under either rule.

## Joint inference

Write the short ATT as $\theta_s$, residual variance as $a=\sigma_{0,s}^2$,
and conditional imbalance as $b=\nu_{0,s}^2$. With $S^2=ab$, the adapter uses

$$
\phi_{S^2,i}=b\phi_{a,i}+a\phi_{b,i},\qquad
\widehat V=\frac{1}{n^2}\sum_i(\phi_i-\bar\phi)(\phi_i-\bar\phi)',
\quad\phi_i=(\phi_{\theta,i},\phi_{a,i},\phi_{b,i})'.
$$

The external DRDID IF is an unscaled unit-level contribution. It is neither
divided by $n$ before assembly nor replaced by the DML ATT IF. For a fixed
sensitivity factor $k=\sqrt{\rho^2\,cf.y\,cf.d/(1-cf.d)}$, the endpoint IFs are
$\phi_{\theta,i}\pm k\phi_{S^2,i}/(2\sqrt{S^2})$. Their standard errors include
the cross-covariance between the external ATT and the sensitivity moments.

`confidence_bounds()` defaults to the envelope over all confounding no stronger
than the supplied sensitivity values. Use `max = FALSE` for the interval at
exactly those values. Its `level` parameter supplies the one-sided normal
quantile: at zero sensitivity, `level = 0.95` uses `qnorm(0.95)`; use
`level = 0.975` to recover the usual two-sided 95% normal interval. Accordingly,
the source ATT and analytic SE, rather than the original CI endpoints, are the
zero-sensitivity invariant.

Valid hybrid inference requires jointly asymptotically linear estimators on
the same units and target population, appropriate moments and overlap, and
valid nuisance estimation on each side. DRDID's double robustness for the short
ATT does **not** imply double robustness for the entire sensitivity analysis.
The DML outcome and propensity functions used by the sensitivity moments need
their own consistency/rate conditions. Causal interpretation also requires the
long-model identifying and sensitivity assumptions in the DiD paper.

## Object structure and benchmarks

| Component | Content |
|---|---|
| `results$main$treat[[1]]` | Hybrid estimates, IFs, and `joint.covariance` in order ATT, residual variance, imbalance |
| `coefs$main$treat` | External ATT and analytic IF standard error |
| `fits` | Cross-fitted DML nuisance predictions |
| `auxiliary_dml_results` | Original DML results retained for diagnostics |
| `external_fit` | Supplied DRDID object |
| `adapter_data` | Frozen wide panel data, IDs, weights, design matrix and input mapping |
| `adapter_info` | Source method, reconstruction version, fold IDs and source propensity diagnostics |
| `refit_spec` | Source settings and DML options used for benchmark refits |

The source propensities in `adapter_info$diagnostics$propensity` are reconstructed
for verification; they are not propensities extracted from the DRDID output or
the cross-fitted DML propensity predictions.

Each benchmark removes the named design columns and re-estimates **both** DRDID
and the DML sensitivity moments, using the frozen units and the same fold seed.
The reduced ATT and IF therefore remain DRDID quantities. This works after
`saveRDS()`/`readRDS()` without evaluating the original source or adapter call.
Learner specifications must themselves remain usable after serialization.
Benchmark group labels must be unique, including labels generated for unnamed
groups. Duplicate labels produce an error before any benchmark is fitted.
